title: Count Reachable Workstations (DFS)
real_world_story: Before assigning work, the fleet controller must know which workstations a dock can actually serve. Regions of the floor can be sealed off by machine clusters, so some workstations may be impossible to reach from this dock.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Factory floor grid where 0 is a free aisle, 1 is a blocked region and 2 is a workstation
real_world_connection.query_represents: The dock cell from which robots depart
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Following one corridor as far as possible before backing out, to visit every cell the dock can reach

problem_statement: Given an R x C factory floor grid of 0 (free aisle), 1 (blocked region) and 2 (workstation), and the dock cell (sr, sc), determine how many workstation cells can be reached from the dock using 4-directional moves. A workstation is reachable when there is a route from the dock that never enters a blocked cell. The dock cell itself counts as reachable when it is a workstation.
task: Return the number of workstation cells reachable from the dock.
input_format: The first line contains two integers R and C. The next R lines each contain C integers (0, 1 or 2) describing the floor. The final line contains two integers sr sc.
output_format: Print a single integer: the number of reachable workstation cells. Print 0 when no workstation (including the dock) is reachable.

examples.explanation: From (0,0) the robot can walk to (0,1) -> (1,1) -> (1,2) -> (2,2). Both (0,0) and (2,2) are workstations, and (2,0) is sealed off by the blocked cells (1,0) and (2,1).

expected_algorithm.name: Graph DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: The question is reachability rather than distance, so a depth-first traversal that marks visited cells and counts workstation cells is enough.

hint: Walk from the dock and never enter a blocked cell.
Remember every cell you have already visited so no cell is processed twice.
Count the cells you visit whose value marks them as a workstation.
real_world_takeaway: Reachability queries tell a fleet controller which workstations a robot can serve at all, so jobs are never assigned to an unreachable target.
